skill.name: runtime-agents
skill.description: Create, list, preview, update, enable, disable, and delete reusable runtime sub-agents.
skill.runtime_agent_intent_routing:
1. LIST (list, view, inspect, show): - Call `list_runtime_agents` only. - Return the listed agent summaries to the user. - Never expose full system prompts in a list response.
2. PREVIEW (preview, read, open, inspect content, show agent): - Call `preview_runtime_agent(id)` only. - Return the full definition, including the system prompt, to the user.
3. CREATE (create, add, new): - Call `list_capabilities` first when capability selection is unclear. - Call `create_runtime_agent(name, description, systemPrompt, capabilityIds, maxSteps?, enabled?)`. - Use a concise kebab-case-friendly name and a routing description the supervisor can match later. - Only choose capability ids from the grantable catalog (`list_capabilities`). - The tool writes the runtime system prompt to `data/prompts/{id}.xml` (Docker-persisted volume). JSON stores `promptSourceKey: {id}` and a bootstrap snapshot; the XML file is the runtime source of truth. - After create or enable, tell the user the bot and scheduler pick up routing changes automatically within a few seconds (soft graph recompile). - If the user will schedule cron jobs for the new agent id, note that the scheduler process may need a restart before cron targeting accepts the new id. - Configure skill auto-attachment triggers in each skill file's `` block with `module` on the root `` tag.
4. UPDATE (edit, update, change, rewrite, enable, disable): - Call `preview_runtime_agent(id)` first when the current definition is unknown. - Then call `update_runtime_agent(id, ...)` with the replacement fields. - When `systemPrompt` is updated, the tool rewrites `data/prompts/{id}.xml`; JSON keeps the bootstrap snapshot. - Legacy chat-created agents with inline-only prompts migrate to a prompt file on the first `systemPrompt` update.
5. DELETE (remove, delete): - Require explicit user confirmation before deleting. - Call `delete_runtime_agent(id)`.
